title: Transient native mailbox relay unavailability DL560→Central (503 send, 423 read) on d3499b97; recovery worked, cause unknown
outcome: The cause of the brief cross-machine mailbox relay outages seen from DL560 on 2026-11-08 is identified or bounded: the home-side state, load, or a relay defect. If it is a defect, it is fixed so that ordinary sends and reads don't fail transiently under normal load.
acceptance: Record a code-first comparison of relay-principal-* and host-qualified native-session sends, tracing principal resolution, conversation/home selection, peer/client reuse and applicable request budgets against the incident build. Distinguish any real path differences from the two-sample correlation.

Trace the reported 423 and exact 'native mailbox relay response unavailable' 503 to their producing boundaries, including applicable budgets and pre/post-append uncertainty. Record the three supplied occurrences and existing load evidence without live probes, store queries or other sessions' mailbox reads, and do not claim a runtime cause absent supporting evidence.

If a defect is confirmed, record the causal evidence and Kimi-concurred plan before edits, repair the existing owning mechanism without weakening authentication, outcome-unknown or same-key recovery semantics, and provide meaningful focused checks, the required independent review pair and exact final full gate before landing. If no defect is established from the authorized evidence, record a bounded no-change disposition, excluded explanations, remaining missing evidence and the responsible supported follow-up instead of inventing a cause or changing behavior.

completion.summary: Completed code-first relay failure triage with a bounded no-change disposition: common authenticated RPC path and budgets traced; specific historical home refusal cause remains unavailable, and supported recurrence evidence owner recorded.
